This is a beta. Install it with [BRAT](https://github.com/TfTHacker/obsidian42-brat) by adding `anupchavan/obsidian-custom-views` as a beta plugin. The community store stays on 0.5.1 until this is promoted.

### Template diagnostics
- The HTML, CSS and JavaScript editors now check your code as you type. A line with a problem is tinted, the exact spot is underlined, and a banner at the end of the line gives the message. Click the banner for every message on that line and a hint on how to fix it; click a message to select that spot.
- Checks cover unclosed `{{ }}` and `{% %}`, `if`/`for`/`set`/`base` block structure, expression syntax (reported at the bracket that's never closed), unknown filters, functions and methods with "did you mean" suggestions, and filter arguments written as `date("…")`.
- Property names that no note in the vault has are flagged as warnings, with case-sensitive suggestions (`PHOTO` → `photo`).
- CSS brace balance and missing `:` in declarations, and JavaScript syntax errors, are reported in their editors. Template placeholders inside CSS and JavaScript don't count as errors.
- An error thrown when the preview runs a script appears on the line that threw, in the view's JavaScript or in an inline `<script>` in the template.
- New problems wait for a short pause in typing, so half-written expressions don't flash errors. Fixing a problem clears it at once.

### Improvements
- Template editors in settings grow with their code up to 24em instead of always taking that height, so short templates no longer leave empty space below.
- Autocomplete and the problem popover are no longer clipped by the settings modal.
- The code editors no longer show "HTML template" and similar labels as hover tooltips. Screen readers still announce them.

### Maintenance
- Consolidated the test suite: redundant cases became tables and tests that could not fail were removed, with coverage unchanged or higher in every file (#27).

### Validation
- 1,330 automated tests pass, plus lint, browser typechecking and the production build.
- The diagnostics were checked in Obsidian desktop during development and in a browser harness with Obsidian's light and dark theme variables. Mobile was not tested on a device.
